title: Entanglement Entropy of Free Fermions in Timelike Slices
abstract: Defines the entanglement entropy of free-fermion states in an arbitrary spacetime slice of a discrete set of points, in particular timelike slices: a set of times t_n = n tau on one site. Zero-temperature ground states show volume law for tau >> 2 pi / E_0, (1/3) ln t at tau = tau_0 and (1/6) ln t below it, resembling Calabrese-Cardy for nonchiral and chiral fermions. Finite temperature, non-eigenstates and generic spacetime slices also treated; area-to-volume transition as the slice turns timelike.
key_claims: A REAL-valued entropy of Heisenberg-picture operators sampled at discrete times on one site; not the complex pseudo-entropy of PAPER-139
Log scaling with coefficient 1/6 or 1/3 depending on the sampling interval
relevance_note: Prior-art check for HYP-2026-032's definition-agreement leg: this is a DIFFERENT object (real, discrete time sampling, no imaginary part), so it does not pre-empt the comparison of the two Doi et al. lattice definitions at finite n. Cited as the nearest lattice precedent.
